99: \begin{abstract}
100: We extend the short presentation due to [Borel '53] of the cohomology
101: ring of a generalized flag manifold to a relatively short presentation
102: of the cohomology of any of its Schubert varieties. Our result is
103: stated in a root-system uniform manner by introducing the {\it
104: essential set of a Coxeter group element}, generalizing and giving a
105: new characterization of [Fulton '92]'s definition for permutations.
106: Further refinements are obtained in type $A$.
107: \end{abstract}

115: \section{Introduction}
116: \label{intro-section}
117: %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
118: 
119: %The first main result of this paper is Theorem 1.1 below.  We first
120: %explain here some of the background and motivation behind it.
121: % AY: I know we've talked about this before, but given there's an abstract,
122: % this sentence seems a little funny to me. What else were we planning to do
123: % but to explain the background and motivation for our result?
124: 
125: The cohomology of the generalized flag manifold $G/B$, for any complex
126: semisimple algebraic group $G$ and Borel subgroup $B$, has a classical
127: presentation due to Borel \cite{Borel}.  Pick a maximal torus
128: $T\subset B\subset G$, choose a field $\Bbbk$ of characteristic zero, and let
129: $V=\Bbbk\otimes_{\ZZ} X(T)$, where $X(T)$ is the coweight lattice of
130: $T$.  Let $\Bbbk[V]:=\Sym(V^{\star})$ be the symmetric algebra for
131: $V^{\star}$; it naturally carries an action of the Weyl group $W :=
132: N_G(T)/T$.  Furthermore let $\Bbbk[V]^W$ be the ring of $W$-invariants
133: of $\Bbbk[V]$, and $\Bbbk[V]^W_+$ the ideal of $\Bbbk[V]$ generated by
134: the $W$-invariants of positive degree.  A classical theorem of Borel
135: \cite{Borel} states that
136: \begin{equation}
137: \label{Borel-presentation}
138: H^*(G/B,\Bbbk) \cong \Bbbk[V]/(\Bbbk[V]^W_+).
139: \end{equation}
140: %This presentation is proved by showing that $\Bbbk[V]^W_+$ is the kernel of the
141: %surjective map $\Sym(V^\star) \rightarrow H^*(G/B)$ that sends a torus
142: %weight $\lambda \in V^{\star}$ to the first Chern class of the equivariant
143: %line bundle ${\mathcal L}_\lambda$ on $G/B$; see the original paper
144: %\cite{Borel} or, e.g., \cite[\S III.4]{Hiller} for further details.  
145: 
146: A desirable feature of Borel's presentation is its shortness: since $W$
147: acts on $V^\star$ as a finite reflection group, by Chevalley's Theorem,
148: the $W$-invariants $\Bbbk[V]^W$ are a polynomial algebra
149: $\Bbbk[f_1,\ldots,f_n]$, where $n:=\dim_\Bbbk V$ is the rank of
150: $G$ \cite[Section~3.5]{humphreys}.  Hence Borel's presentation shows
151: that $H^\star(G/B)$ is a complete intersection as it has $n$ generators and
152: $n$ relations.
153: 
154:  There is a second way to describe $H^{\star}(G/B)$ arising from
155:  a cell decomposition of $G/B$. One has
156: $$
157: \begin{array}{rll}
158: G&=\bigsqcup_{w \in W} BwB & \text{(Bruhat decomposition)}\\
159: G/B&=\bigsqcup_{w \in W} X_w^\circ & \text{(Schubert cell decomposition), with}\\ 
160: X_w^\circ&:=BwB/B \cong \CC^{\ell(w)} &\text{ (open Schubert cell)}.  
161: \end{array}
162: $$ Here $\ell(w)$ denotes the Coxeter group length of $w$ under the
163: Coxeter system $(W,S)$, where $S$ are the reflections in the simple
164: roots $\Pi$ among the positive roots $\Phi^+$ 
165: within the natural root system $\Phi$ associated to our Lie pinning.  
166: This gives a
167: $CW$-decomposition for $G/B$ in which all cells have even real
168: dimension.  Hence the fundamental homology classes $[X_w]$ of their
169: closures $X_w:=\overline{X_w^\circ}$, the {\bf Schubert varieties},
170: form a $\ZZ$-basis for the integral homology $H_\star(G/B)$, and their
171: (Kronecker) duals $\sigma_w:=[X_w]^\star$ form the dual $\ZZ$-basis for
172: the integral cohomology $H^\star(G/B)$.
173:

175: for $H^\star(X_w)$; see also \cite[Cor. 4.4]{Carrell} and

204: Therefore, a basic question is to request more efficient generating
205: sets for $I_w$.  For type $A_{n-1}$, earlier work
206: \cite{GasharovReiner} reduced the $|W|=n!$ upper bound on the number
207: of generators for $I_w$ to a polynomial bound of $n^2$ for the class
208: of Schubert varieties $X_w$ \emph{defined by inclusions}; this class
209: includes all smooth $X_w$. Moreover, for a certain subclass of smooth
210: Schubert varieties $X_w$ considered originally by Ding
211: \cite{Ding1,Ding2}, they gave a smaller generating set for these $I_w$
212: having only $n$ generators.  This latter result was applied in
213: \cite{DevelinMartinReiner} to classify these varieties up to
214: isomorphism and homeomorphism (the generating set \eqref{first-I-def}
215: having proved too unwieldy). One motivation for this work arises from
216: the desire to extend this classification to general Schubert varieties of
217: type $A$.  Experience suggests that presentations for $I_w$ that are
218: as simple as possible are best for this purpose.
219: 
220: The question of finding 
221: simple presentations of $I_w$ for other root systems appears to 
222: have been less studied.

17: 
18: Here, if \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), the parameters are

28: \]

46: ## 2. Evidence reported by the authors
47: 
48: The authors state that they verified the conjecture computationally for all bigrassmannian permutations satisfying
49: 
50: \[
51: r\leq 4,\qquad n-r\leq 5.
52: \]
53: 
54: **Primary-source location:** lines 1501–1502.
55: 
56: ## 3. Stronger suspected formulation
57: 
58: Set \(M=J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\), and let \(\Lambda_+\) denote the positive-degree part of the ring of symmetric functions. The authors further conjecture that
59: 
60: \[
61: M/\Lambda_+M
62: \]
63: 
64: requires \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) generators. They suspect the stronger structural statement
65: 
66: \[
67: M/\Lambda_+M\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}.
68: \]
69: 
70: This is presented in prose rather than as a second numbered conjecture. The authors write that a proof had eluded them.
71: 
72: **Primary-source location:** lines 1517–1552.
73: 
74: ## 4. Consequence of the conjecture
75: 
76: Take \(n=4m\) and the family for which \(a=b=m\). If the minimality conjecture is true, the corresponding ideal requires
77: 
78: \[
79: \binom{2m}{m}
80: \sim \frac{4^m}{\sqrt{\pi m}}
81: =\frac{\sqrt{2}^{\,n+2}}{\sqrt{\pi n}}
82: \]
83: 
84: generators. This gives an exponential lower bound and shows that uniformly short presentations of \(H^*(X_w)\) cannot be expected in general, even in type \(A\).
85: 
86: **Primary-source location:** lines 1504–1515; see also the introductory discussion at lines 355–364.
87: 
88: ## 5. Related open question
89: 
90: The final section asks:
91: 
92: > Can one find a minimal generating set for the ideal \(I_w\) in type \(A_{n-1}\)?
93: 
94: The authors ask whether this can at least be done for subclasses already known to admit generating sets of size \(n^2\), including:
95: 
96: 1. Schubert varieties defined by inclusions, characterized there by avoidance of
97:    \(\{4231,35142,42513,351624\}\);
98: 2. smooth Schubert varieties, characterized by avoidance of \(\{3412,4231\}\).
99: 
100: This is an open question, not another formally labeled conjecture.
101: 
102: **Primary-source location:** lines 1897–1935.
103: 
104: ## Classification summary
105: 
106: | Item | Status in the paper |
107: |---|---|
108: | Minimality of both Theorem 5.4 generating sets for \(J_v\) | Formally labeled conjecture |
109: | \(M/\Lambda_+M\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\) | Stronger suspected statement in prose |
110: | Minimal generating sets for general \(I_w\) in type \(A\) | Formally labeled open question |
